function.name: read_files
function.description:
Inspect and read files/folders in the project. One tool, several modes; pick the mode for the job.
- mode 'read' (default): read file contents with 1-based line numbers. Pass start_line/end_line to read a slice of one file when output is long or you need a later part. Pass several paths to read multiple small files in one call.
- mode 'list': list the immediate contents of one or more folders.
- mode 'tree': show a folder tree under a path up to max_depth levels (skips .git, .venv, __pycache__, .simpleagent).
- mode 'glob': find files whose names match a pattern (e.g. '*.py') under a path. Requires pattern.
- mode 'info': basic metadata (type, size, line count, modified time) for one or more paths.
Use this instead of terminal commands like Get-Content, type, cat, dir, ls for inspecting files.

paths.description: One or more paths relative to the project root. For 'tree' and 'glob' the first path is the root (use '.' for the project root).

start_line.description: First line to read, 1-based inclusive. Only used in 'read' mode with a single file.

end_line.description: Last line to read, 1-based inclusive. Only used in 'read' mode with a single file.

max_depth.description: Folder levels to include in 'tree' mode.

pattern.description: Filename pattern for 'glob' mode, e.g. '*.py' or '*.md'.

function.name: search_codebase
function.description: Search the project for a word or regular expression (case-insensitive). Returns matching lines as 'path:line_number: line'. Use file_glob to scope to a file type (e.g. '*.py'). Results are capped; narrow the pattern or use file_glob if there are too many.

pattern.description: Word or regular expression to search for, case-insensitive.

path.description: Folder to search in, relative to the project root. Defaults to the project root.

file_glob.description: Optional filename pattern to scope the search, e.g. '*.py' or '*.md'.

function.name: editor
function.description:
Create or change files in the project. One tool, four operations; pick 'operation' for the job.
- 'write': create or overwrite a file with full content.
- 'patch': apply one or more targeted edits to an existing file. Each replacement must have a unique old_text (add surrounding lines if it appears more than once). The whole file is kept; only the matched text is swapped. To insert, match an anchor line and include it plus the new text in new_text.
- 'delete': delete a file (refuses to delete a folder).
- 'move': move or rename a file from source to destination.

path.description: Target file path relative to the project root. Used by 'write', 'patch', and 'delete'.

content.description: The full text content to write. Used by 'write'.

replacements.description: Targeted edits for 'patch'. Each item swaps a unique old_text for new_text.

old_text.description: The exact text to find (must be unique in the file).

new_text.description: The text to replace it with.

function.name: run_command
function.description: Run a shell command in the project folder. Use this for builds, tests, git, and any script not covered by the file/web tools. Read-only commands (dir, git status, git diff, git log, uv run, uv sync, etc.) run automatically. Commands that change files or system state (git push, pip install, remove-item, redirects, etc.) require approval, and dangerous patterns are blocked. Do NOT use this to read or list files - use read_files instead; file-inspection commands are blocked here.

function.name: fetch_web
function.description:
Reach the web. Two modes, picked by what you pass:
- Pass 'url' to fetch one page or data endpoint (HTTPS only; local/private addresses are blocked). JSON is pretty-printed and HTML is stripped to text. Pass 'prompt' to get a focused answer distilled from the page instead of the full content.
- Pass 'query' (no url) to run a web search via Tavily: returns titles, URLs, and snippets plus a short summary. Use search_type='news' for current events, search_depth='advanced' for more relevant results, include_domains to restrict to trusted sources, and time_limit to filter by age.
Follow a search result by fetching its url in detail.

url.description: Full http or https URL to fetch. If given, fetches that page (search params are ignored).

query.description: Search query. Used when no url is given.

prompt.description: Optional question to answer from the fetched page. Only used with 'url'.

max_results.description: Maximum search results to return (1-10). Default 5. Used with 'query'.

search_type.description: 'text' for general web search (default), 'news' for current events. Used with 'query'.

search_depth.description: Search depth: 'basic' (default), 'advanced' (more relevant), 'fast' or 'ultra-fast'. Used with 'query'.

include_domains.description: Domains to restrict search to, e.g. ['python.org', 'github.com']. Used with 'query'.

exact_match.description: If true, only return results containing the exact quoted phrase(s). Used with 'query'.

function.name: memory
function.description: Update your long-term memory, which is loaded into context every session. Provide the FULL new content; it replaces the old file, so keep everything you want plus the new fact and drop anything stale. Use scope 'global' for durable facts about the user (max 2000 chars), 'project' for durable facts about the current project (max 6000 chars). Keep it concise markdown.

scope.description: Which memory to update: 'global' (about the user) or 'project' (about this project).

content.description: The full new memory content as concise markdown.

function.name: skills
function.description:
Manage your reusable skills (short markdown runbooks you write and improve). One tool, four actions:
- 'list': list all saved skills (names + descriptions).
- 'read': load the full steps of a skill by name (do this before a task a skill covers).
- 'save': create or update a skill. Keep it concise (max 4000 chars). Use scope 'project' or 'global'.
- 'delete': delete a skill that is stale or wrong.

name.description: Skill name (lowercase-hyphen, e.g. 'add-a-tool'). Used by 'read', 'save', and 'delete'.

description.description: One line describing when to use this skill. Used by 'save'.

content.description: The procedure as markdown: when to use, steps, pitfalls, how to verify. Used by 'save'.

scope.description: 'project' for a project-specific skill, 'global' for a general skill. Used by 'save'.

function.name: sessions
function.description:
Recall past conversations saved in this project. One tool, two actions:
- 'search': search past sessions for a word or regular expression (case-insensitive); returns short matching snippets with the session name and date, newest first.
- 'read': read one past session in full by its name (use after search to see the full context).

query.description: Word or regular expression to search for. Used by 'search'.

name.description: Session name, with or without the .json extension. Used by 'read'.

function.name: ask_question
function.description: Ask the user a clarifying question with 2 to 5 selectable options. Use this only when you need a key decision before proceeding and guessing wrong would be costly — not for every small question.

question.description: The single question to ask the user.
